_about: Stable facts about each resort. Prices, closing dates and events live in the season file (data/season-2027.json). Ratings are 1-5 stars from resort guides; temperatures are approximate February averages (high / low), not a forecast.

snow: 630 m in the village, 2,000 m+ on the Penken; Hintertux glacier included in the pass
temp: in the village; around −4° high on the Penken
beginners: Beginner area on the Ahorn; many runs are red
snowboard: Vans Penken Park, one of the best parks in the Alps
apres: Ice Bar, Brück'n Stadl, big late-afternoon parties
compare.insurance: No insurance sold with the pass; mountain rescue is billed separately. The EHIC covers healthcare, not rescue.

snow: Low area (620–1957 m); relies heavily on snowmaking, especially in March
beginners: Lots of wide, easy blues, good for progressing
snowboard: Several parks; wide runs with few flats
expert: Plenty of easy and intermediate terrain, little that is hard
apres: Söll and Ellmau have lively Austrian après-ski
compare.insurance: No insurance sold with the pass; mountain rescue is billed separately. The EHIC covers healthcare, not rescue.

snow: 1,860 m in the village, Pic Blanc at 3,330 m
temp: in the village; very sunny resort
beginners: Lots of greens, beginner zones and a beginner pass (€26/day)
snowboard: Snowpark and wide terrain; a few flat paths
compare.insurance: Carré Neige ~€3.50/day with the pass: covers rescue and unused lessons.

snow: Glacier at 3,600 m; snow guaranteed up top
area: Grand Domaine; the Supernova link reaches Alpe d'Huez
beginners: Easy runs up high; the run back to the village is hard, so beginners ride the gondola down. Beginner pass €26
snowboard: One of the best-known snowparks in France
apres: Very young crowd, bars all along the main street
compare.insurance: Optional insurance with the pass (~€3–4/day). The EHIC covers healthcare, not rescue.

snow: Morzine at 1,000 m (rain risk in the village); Avoriaz at 1,800 m
area: Portes du Soleil, France and Switzerland
beginners: Better for beginners in Avoriaz than in Morzine
snowboard: Avoriaz has a freestyle tradition; lots of drag lifts and flats across the area
expert: Le Mur Suisse and varied terrain
apres: Morzine: Tibetan Café, Le Ridge; Avoriaz is quieter
wind: Many runs among trees; frequent fog
compare.insurance: Carré Neige with the pass. On the Swiss side the EHIC applies, rescue cover does not.

snow: Village at 2,300 m, the highest in Europe; snow into May
temp: in the village; the coldest resort on the list
area: Val Thorens–Orelle (600 km with the 3 Vallées)
beginners: Free beginner lifts and wide blues; cold and wind make it harder
snowboard: VT Park and wide runs with few flats
expert: Cime Caron and access to all of the 3 Vallées
apres: La Folie Douce, Malaysia, Frog & Roastbeef
wind: Above the tree line: lifts close in high wind
compare.insurance: Carré Neige ~€3.50/day with the pass: covers rescue and unused lessons.

snow: Village at 1,500 m, top at 2,823 m; good snowmaking
area: Via Lattea, with Sestriere and Montgenèvre
beginners: Beginner area on the Sportinia plateau; cheap lessons
snowboard: Park in Sestriere; some flat links
expert: Huge area with lots of varied terrain
apres: Known for lively après-ski, popular with British skiers
wind: Some high links close in wind
compare.insurance: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory in Italy since 2022 (a few euros a day with the pass).

snow: Pass at 1,883 m and the Presena glacier at 3,016 m
beginners: Wide, easy runs; some of the cheapest group lessons
snowboard: Small snowpark; flat areas on the pass
expert: Little challenge away from the glacier
apres: Few bars; Paradice Music parties on some dates
compare.insurance: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory in Italy since 2022 (a few euros a day with the pass).

snow: Village at 2,100 m, but Pyrenees snow varies a lot from year to year
beginners: Wide runs and cheap ski schools; beginner pass €45.50
expert: Good for a day or two of challenge
apres: Main street packed with bars and clubs until late
wind: Port d'Envalira is exposed; the road can close in snow
compare.insurance: The EHIC is not valid in Andorra (outside the EU). Buy the pass insurance or travel insurance with winter sports.

snow: Village at 1,710 m, runs up to 2,640 m; Pyrenees snow varies
area: All of Grandvalira (same area as Pas de la Casa)
beginners: One of the best schools for learning in English; easy zones up high
expert: Same as Pas de la Casa
apres: Fat Albert and Aspen Bar; lively but calmer than Pas de la Casa
compare.insurance: The EHIC is not valid in Andorra (outside the EU). Buy the pass insurance or travel insurance with winter sports.

snow: The best snow in the Pyrenees, thanks to Atlantic weather
beginners: The Beret plateau is great for learning; lessons are expensive
expert: Lots of off-piste and quality blacks
apres: More upmarket; late dinners in Vielha and Baqueira
compare.insurance: The EHIC covers healthcare in Spain, not rescue. Optional insurance with the pass.

snow: High (2,100–3,300 m), but a southern climate: snow varies a lot from year to year
beginners: Borreguiles area is good for learning; cheap lessons
apres: Bars in Pradollano, busy at weekends
wind: Strong wind often closes the top lifts
compare.insurance: The EHIC covers healthcare in Spain, not rescue. Optional insurance with the pass.

fit.text: The best learning area on the list, lots of sun, lively après-ski and a 16 km black for experienced skiers. Mid-range price.
Guaranteed snow, top après-ski, great for skiing and snowboarding. Cold and wind can make beginners' first days hard, and it's one of the priciest.

fit.tag: Learn and party on a budget
fit.text: Excellent ski school, Andorra prices and lively après-ski without the excess of Pas de la Casa. The transfer is over 2h45.
Wide blues to learn on, big parties and a short transfer from Munich. The risk is snow, as it's low; best in late January and February.
Cheap lessons and drinks and very lively nights. Snow is less reliable than in the high Alps, and experienced skiers run out of terrain faster.
Great for beginners and one of the cheapest, but little nightlife and not much challenge for experienced skiers.

fitFootnote: Les 2 Alpes is great for snowboarding and nightlife, but beginners ride the gondola back to the village. Sauze d'Oulx is a strong option if there's a flight to Turin on your dates. Baqueira has the best snow in the Pyrenees but is expensive and less lively. Sierra Nevada is the closest to Portugal but has the least reliable snow.
